extracted.intended_audience: Referees / peer reviewers for Humanities & Social Sciences Communications (academics in humanities, social and behavioural sciences)
extracted.subtask_description: Official referee instructions for reviewers assessing manuscripts submitted to Humanities & Social Sciences Communications; covers criteria for publication, how to write reports, conduct and procedural requirements (anonymity, timing, conflicts, AI use).

rubrics_metrics.name: Within journal's scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Report research that is within the journal’s scope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Familiarise yourself with the journal’s aims and scope. If a paper has been sent out for peer review this implies the Editors consider it to be within the journal’s scope. Papers inappropriate for a Guest-edited Collection may be considered for the general section; Editors will communicate such decisions to authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear and valid research question
rubrics_metrics.description: Pose a clear and valid research question.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the paper poses a well-defined question. In your report, note whether the core claims are clearly conveyed in the abstract and conclusions and whether the paper poses a clear and valid research question.

rubrics_metrics.name: Academically sound methodology and analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Be academically sound in methodology and analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the methodology and analysis are appropriate and robust. Comment on sufficiency of methodological detail, whether methods are appropriate to the question, and whether any aspects are outside your expertise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate evidence or reasoning for conclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide appropriate evidence or reasoning for the conclusions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check that claims are fully supported by argument(s) and any associated data. If claims are not convincing, identify what further evidence is needed and describe flaws (logical, analytical, ethical or other) that would prohibit publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contribution to the literature
rubrics_metrics.description: Make a contribution to the literature — irrespective of magnitude.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The requirement is that a paper should report something specific and not simply repeat what is already known. Indicate whether the paper makes a contribution; if you feel it simply restates known work, provide evidence and identify major papers that suggest otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation and standard English
rubrics_metrics.description: Be presented in an intelligible fashion and in standard English.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comment on clarity, structure and accessibility of the text. Reviewers are not required to comment on minor phraseological or grammatical issues unless they are essential to understanding; invite feedback on logic and narrative coherence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess exclusively against publication criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviews and editorial assessments should be based exclusively on the journal's criteria for publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not base recommendations on perceived importance, significance or impact; the research community will judge these after publication. You may comment on significance as extra information for authors, but recommendations must be grounded in the stated criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation types and rationale
rubrics_metrics.description: Referees are asked to recommend acceptance, revisions, or rejection and provide supporting arguments for the decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide information on which an editorial decision should be based and set out arguments for and against publication. Editors may consult referees further if reports disagree; be willing to provide follow-up advice if requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accept / Accept in principle / Request revision / Reject (editorial decision types)
rubrics_metrics.description: Possible editorial outcomes: Accept outright; Accept in principle; Request revision; Reject outright.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors make the final decision after considering reports. Recommend 'reject' if one or more of the journal’s publication criteria are not satisfied and are unlikely to be satisfied even with revision. Do not use subjective 'major'/'minor' labels; focus on degree to which criteria are met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Willingness to review revisions
rubrics_metrics.description: When agreeing to review a paper, commit to review subsequent revisions as well where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors may involve new referees if necessary. Editors will not send resubmitted papers to referees if authors have not made a serious attempt to address criticisms. Be aware that agreeing implies commitment to follow-up review unless otherwise arranged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer selection factors
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors choose appropriate referees based on expertise, specific recommendations and previous experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invitations to review are confidential. Authors may recommend reviewers on submission. The journal does not rely on a fixed reviewer pool; Editors seek the most appropriate experts for assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constructive and instructive feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviews should instruct authors how to strengthen their manuscript and be constructive and instructive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide suggestions for modifications (including experiments, data, additional discussion) that could help make the work suitable for publication. Suggestions should be limited to what can reasonably be addressed in a revision and exclude changes that would significantly change the scope of the work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anonymity in reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors and reviewers should keep their own identities anonymous (referee anonymity).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The journal does not release reviewers' identities to authors or other reviewers unless reviewers request identification. Reviewers should not identify themselves to authors without the Editorial Office's knowledge; if they wish to reveal their identities, do so via the publishing office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objectivity and appropriate tone
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviews should be conducted objectively and personal criticism of the author is inappropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Express views clearly with supporting arguments and references; avoid defamatory or libellous comments. Avoid language that causes needless offence. Editors transmit comments intended for authors as written except in rare cases where offensive language or confidential info must be removed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declaration and handling of competing interests
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers should declare any competing interests in the notes to the Editor and decline reviews where they believe a competing interest prevents objectivity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Competing interests include competitive, collaborative, or other relationships with authors, companies, or institutions. If in doubt or if a past relationship exists, draw attention to it; such connections do not automatically invalidate a report, but should be declared so Editors can weigh them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality and consulting others
rubrics_metrics.description: Treat the review process as strictly confidential and do not discuss manuscripts with anyone not directly involved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is acceptable to consult colleagues but they must be identified to the Editor. Consulting external experts may be acceptable but check with the editorial office first to avoid involving excluded persons. Do not use unpublished manuscript information in your own work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Passing review requests to colleagues
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers must not pass a review request to a colleague without contacting the journal first.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you wish to nominate an alternate reviewer, contact the journal rather than forwarding the manuscript or invitation directly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Key arguments or results (report element)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide an overview of the key messages of the paper in your own words, highlighting what you find interesting or notable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usually summarise in a short paragraph so Editors and authors understand your reading of the manuscript's main contributions and claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Validity (report element)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate the soundness and robustness of the research question and conclusions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you feel there are flaws (logical, analytical, ethical or other) that prohibit publication, describe them in detail so editors and authors can assess the severity and whether remediation is possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data and/or methodology (report element)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess the validity of the approach, the quality of the data, and the quality of presentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review all data including supplementary information. If aspects are outside your expertise, note this in the report or in comments to the Editor. Comment on access to datasets and materials if inadequate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analytical approach (report element)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess the strength of the analytical approach (e.g., validity and comprehensiveness of statistical tests or logical coherence of arguments).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicate whether statistical tests are appropriate and correctly applied; note if parts are outside your expertise and what further analysis may be required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contribution (report element)
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate whether the paper makes a contribution to the literature, irrespective of perceived magnitude.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you judge the work to simply restate known results, provide citations/evidence. Do not base recommendation on the perceived impact; focus on whether it reports something specific and new.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suggested improvements (report element)
rubrics_metrics.description: Give suggestions for modifications or additions that could help make the manuscript suitable for publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggestions should be feasible within the present scope and avoid recommending work that would significantly change the manuscript's scope. Examples include further experiments, additional analyses, or clarifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity and context (report element)
rubrics_metrics.description: Comment on clarity, accessibility, and whether results are given sufficient context and relation to previous work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invite feedback on narrative logic and structure. You are not required to correct every phrasing error; focus on issues that affect comprehension or interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: References (report element)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether the manuscript references previous literature appropriately and recommend additional directly relevant reading if needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide suggestions for additional literature only if directly relevant to the work under review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Your expertise (report element)
rubrics_metrics.description: State any parts of the manuscript, data or analyses that are outside the scope of your expertise or that you were unable to assess fully.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Helps editors weigh the report and determine whether other reviewers are needed for specific aspects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data and supporting materials availability
rubrics_metrics.description: If authors have not provided adequate access to datasets/materials underpinning their research and this limits your ability to evaluate the paper, note this in your report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess supplementary files and repositories; flag insufficiency so Editor can request further access or clarification.

rubrics_metrics.name: AI use by peer reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer reviewers should not upload manuscripts into generative AI tools and must declare any use of AI tools in evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Generative AI can be unreliable and may expose sensitive or proprietary information. If any part of the evaluation was supported by an AI tool, declare its use transparently in the peer review report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide reports promptly; ideally within approximately 21 days of receiving a manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you anticipate delay, inform the editorial office so authors can be kept informed and alternative referees found if necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Double-anonymous peer review policy
rubrics_metrics.description: The journal uses double-anonymous peer review as default; manuscripts will be sent to referees as received and should be reviewed as such.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors are responsible for deciding whether and to what degree to remove identifying information. Referees may be invited to review files that include identifying information and should review the materials as provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referee anonymity preference
rubrics_metrics.description: The journal prefers reviewers remain anonymous throughout the review process and beyond.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers may request to be identified but should do so via the publishing office. The journal will not confirm or deny speculation about reviewer identities and asks referees to adopt a similar policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editing referees' reports policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors do not edit reviewer reports; comments intended for authors are transmitted as written with rare exceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In rare occasions editors may edit to remove offensive language or comments that reveal confidential information about other matters. Reviewers should avoid comments likely to cause needless offence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance of conflicted referees (editorial selection)
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors aim to avoid referees with recent or ongoing collaborations, those who commented on drafts, direct competitors, those with a history of dispute with authors, or with financial interests in the outcome.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because not all biases are obvious, referees should draw attention to anything that might affect their review. Editors will take such declarations into account when weighing reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Malpractice and integrity
rubrics_metrics.description: The Editor is responsible for maintaining high editorial standards and the journal will take action if it detects malpractice that undermines the integrity of peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report any suspected malpractice or integrity issues to the editorial team; the journal has processes to investigate and act on such concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Online manuscript review submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Referees must submit comments via the journal's online submission system using the link provided in the invitation email.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For help with the manuscript tracking system, contact the editorial office. Do not attempt to transmit review materials by other channels unless instructed.
